NEW DELHI: Population enumeration for the 2027 Census will be conducted across most of India from January 25 to February 28, 2027, with poll-bound states and snow-bound regions excluded from the schedule, the government announced on Friday.According to a notification issued by Mritunjay Kumar Narayan, Registrar General of India and Census Commissioner, the reference date for the census will be midnight on March 1, 2027, PTI reported.The enumeration will not be conducted during this period in Manipur, Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand and Ladakh, or in the snow-bound, non-synchronous areas of Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.The schedule for Manipur will be announced separately. A revisional round will be held from March 1 to March 5, 2027.The government will also offer a self-enumeration option from January 10 to January 24, ahead of the house-to-house population count.Assembly elections are due in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa and Manipur early next year.The 2027 Census, the eighth since Independence, will be conducted in two phases: house listing and housing census, followed by population enumeration.The decennial exercise was originally scheduled for 2021 but was postponed due to the Covid-19 pandemic.The Union Cabinet has approved Rs 11,718 crore for conducting the census.The Registrar General of India had announced last month that house-listing operations for Census 2027 in Manipur had been deferred.The census is a nationwide exercise to collect, compile and analyse information about the population and its demographic, social and economic characteristics.The data provides the government with a detailed picture of the country's population and living conditions.The government has said that information collected during the census will remain confidential and be used only for statistical purposes.India's last census was conducted in 2011, when the country's population stood at 1.21 billion, including 62.32 crore males and 58.75 crore females. The country had 24.95 crore households at the time.
Article Summary: Census 2027 will be conducted in two phases: house listing and housing census, followed by population enumeration. The reference date for the census will be midnight on March 1, 2027. The census is a nationwide exercise to collect, compile and analyse information about the population and its demographic, social and economic characteristics.

Article Title: MP pushes for regulation of AI in healthcare, medical education
Article Text:
BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ajeet Gopchade speaks in Rajya Sabha (File photo/ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India must adopt a robust legal framework to ensure the safe, ethical and accountable use of artificial intelligence in healthcare, clinical research and medical education, where errors can have serious consequences for patients and medical professionals.With the objective to establish a science-based, patient-centric statutory framework that keeps AI under meaningful human control while safeguarding patient safety, informed consent and data governance, Rajya Sabha MP Ajeet Gopchade has urged govt to take up the Artificial Intelligence (Human Health and Medical Education) Regulation Bill, 2026.The objective of this private member Bill is to facilitate responsible and trustworthy innovation, aligned with India’s national priorities, by providing legal clarity, regulatory and confidence in the deployment of artificial intelligence in sectors where human life and dignity are paramount, Gopchade told TOI.The Bill provides for the establishment of an independent regulator, National Authority for Artificial Intelligence in Human Health and Medical Education, with powers to register, scrutinise and approve AI systems, classify risks, establish standards, monitor performance and take enforcement action.``When an AI system causes harm, responsibility must not disappear between hospitals, developers and technology providers.A regulatory authority is needed to oversee system approval, audits, compliance, liability and appropriate compensation’’, Gopchade said.The Bill, a copy of which is available with TOI, empowers the Authority to identify high-risk AI systems based on potential harm, complexity, autonomy and impact on human safety, ethics and rights. Those systems capable of causing death, serious bodily injury, psychological harm, unethical experimentation or other grave consequences would face heightened regulatory scrutiny, it adds.It requires AI systems covered by the Bill to undergo scientific validation in clinical, research or educational settings in India, followed by continuous post-deployment monitoring, bias assessment and performance review.At present, there are existing guidelines covering certain aspects of AI in healthcare, but they may not be legally binding. Earlier, the Indian Council of Medical Research released ethical guidelines to address issues including patient safety, informed consent, transparency and ethical review of AI-based biomedical research and healthcare applications. While the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, cover AI-enabled software that qualifies as a medical device, including safety and performance requirements.
Article Summary: Rajya Sabha MP Ajeet Gopchade has urged govt to take up the Artificial Intelligence (Human Health and Medical Education) Regulation Bill, 2026. The objective of this private member Bill is to facilitate responsible and trustworthy innovation, aligned with India’s national priorities.

Article Title: Global wildlife experts meet at Anant Ambani’s Vantara to strengthen conservation cooperation
Article Text: An Amur tiger has no idea where one country ends and the next begins. Neither does an Oriental stork, a Blakiston’s eagle-owl or a great bustard. Their ranges cross the lines on our maps without pause. But the people working to save them have long struggled with the same problem: the animals move across borders easily, while knowledge about them often doesn’t.Bridging that gap was a key focus of the EARAZA 2026 conference held at Vantara, the wildlife rescue and care centre founded by Anant Ambani in Jamnagar. The event brought together representatives of 98 institutions from 30 countries, along with 29 Indian zoological institutions, to discuss greater cooperation in wildlife conservation.Experts exchanged experiences on coordinated conservation programmes for the Amur tiger, Oriental stork, Blakiston’s eagle-owl and great bustard - species whose survival depends on institutions across countries working with shared knowledge and aligned strategies. A decision taken at one zoological institution, they noted, can influence the prospects of a population thousands of kilometres away.EARAZA president Svetlana Akulova took the argument a step further. She made the case for a global data infrastructure for biodiversity, so that what one institution learns about breeding, health or behaviour can inform decisions at others. Today much of that knowledge stays inside the institution that produced it.Vantara offered a practical start. It is giving all EARAZA members one year of free access to ANTZ, its zoological management platform, which includes an Open Data Exchange that lets institutions share information and collaborate across the network.Technology was a recurring theme throughout the conference. Vantara showcased several ANTZ tools built specifically for wildlife care. One is Vespr, which identifies species from their sounds directly on the device. Another is Smart Egg Analysis, designed to help teams monitor eggs more closely. The third is NFC-enabled logging, which lets caregivers record animal-care rounds digitally. Taken together, they are meant to turn daily observations into usable data.The discussions on animal welfare reflected a similar shift. Instead of treating welfare only as a set of principles, delegates looked at how it can be measured through outcomes for individual animals, so that each animal’s condition becomes the actual test of good care. Sessions also covered building veterinary capacity and preparing institutions for crises.For professionals dealing with specific problems, the Solution Station gave them a place to bring real challenges in wildlife care and conservation and get guidance from experts. The point was to share practical knowledge between institutions rather than just presentations.The conference also looked beyond zoo walls to the public. Wildlife biologist and TV presenter Forrest Galante spoke about the role of mass media in bringing conservation to wider audiences, while other sessions looked at citizen science and how the visitor experience is changing. Conservation, speakers suggested, depends as much on public interest as on expertise.India’s own zoological community had its moment too. The conference marked the release of the Indian Zoo Year Book, Volume 11, the 2026 edition, which underlines the value of careful documentation in a field where records of past successes and failures guide future work.Six Lifetime Achievement Awards were presented to leaders from India and abroad, recognising their contributions to zoological institutions and conservation over the years.As the delegates leave Jamnagar, the main question is whether the connections made this week will last. The tigers, storks and eagle-owls will keep crossing borders as they always have. The aim of the conference was to make sure conservation knowledge does the same.
Article Summary: The EARAZA 2026 conference was held at Vantara, the wildlife rescue and care centre founded by Anant Ambani in Jamnagar. The event brought together representatives of 98 institutions from 30 countries, along with 29 Indian zoological institutions.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Woman who secretly returned from London without informing family found dead in Pune flat
Article Text:
Mugdha Deshmukh, a 34-year-old woman who returned to India, was found dead in Pune this week

Food delivery transactions raise suspicion

Police trace apartment in Pune





PUNE: A 34-year-old woman whose family believed she was studying in London was found dead in a rented apartment in Pune, days after food delivery transactions alerted her parents to the possibility that she had returned to India.Mugdha Deshmukh, a native of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, was found dead inside her apartment at the Lodha Belmondo residential complex in Gahunje, Pimpri Chinchwad, on Thursday. Police said there were no visible injury marks on her body.Mugdha had left for the UK in July 2025 to pursue an MBA. However, without informing her family, she returned to India in August and began living in the rented apartment, police said.According to investigators, Mugdha lived alone in London and had taken up part-time jobs. Her family remained in touch with her through phone calls and messages and believed she was still in the UK.The family became concerned on October 24 when they were unable to contact Mugdha. Her mobile phone was subsequently switched off, her father Avinash Deshmukh stated in a complaint lodged with the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar police earlier this week.Her family then contacted a friend in London, who said the last communication with Mugdha had been through messages on October 22.The friend approached London police to report her missing but was informed that she had left the UK around the end of August, an official said.Concerned about her whereabouts, the family approached Indian authorities and the Indian High Commission for assistance.Mugdha's father also examined her bank statements and noticed several transactions between October 8 and 25 on food delivery and online service platforms.One of the transactions was suspected to have originated from the Osmanpura area of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, leading the family to suspect that she could be in India.The family subsequently approached the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar crime branch, fearing for her safety.The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar police traced Mugdha's location to the Lodha Belmondo complex in Gahunje and alerted their counterparts in Pimpri Chinchwad."We reached the flat she was residing in, gained entry with the help of a keymaker, and found her dead inside," said senior inspector Devendra Chavan of Shirgaon Police in Pimpri Chinchwad.He added that there were no visible injury marks on the body, and her viscera was preserved to ascertain the exact cause of death.During the investigation, police found that Mugdha had rented the apartment in April but began living there only after returning from the UK in August.Police have launched a probe to establish the circumstances surrounding her death.
Article Summary: Mugdha Deshmukh, a native of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, was found dead in Pune. Police said there were no visible injury marks on her body. The 34-year-old had left for the UK in July 2025 to pursue an MBA.

Article Text:

In the eye of a storm

Eight Ajabgarh villas bought for 16.5L each

JAIPUR: The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) Friday registered a preliminary inquiry against senior IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal for allegedly misusing his official position to favour a private company and causing financial losses to the state govt.The state govt formally approved of an investigation against Agrawal earlier in the day. He was serving as an additional chief secretary, industries, when he was put on awaiting posting orders (APO) status Wednesday.At the centre of the probe are alleged irregularities in the purchase of villas by Agrawal and family members.The bureau, in a statement, alleged that Agrawal colluded with the directors of Goyal Fashions Private Limited, which operates hotels and resorts under the brand name ‘Ananta’, to secure undue benefits for the company.These allegedly included relaxations in conditions governing resort construction, approvals without verification of mandatory certificates and a special concessional financial package.The bureau said preliminary investigations also found that Agrawal colluded with the company’s directors to buy villas at its Ananta resorts in his own name and those of his family members. In March 2026, he allegedly purchased 20 villas at the company’s Bujhda resort in Udaipur, besides acquiring villas at its resort at Ajabgarh in Alwar district.According to information gathered during preliminary investigations, Sikhar Agrawal and his IPS officer wife Prashakha Mathur purchased 10 villas each at the Bujhda resort in Udaipur for Rs 15 lakh apiece. At the Ajabgarh resort in Alwar, eight villas were purchased in their names for Rs 16.5 lakh each.Their two sons acquired four villas at approximately Rs 15 lakh each, and an additional four were acquired in the name of other relatives for approximately Rs 16.5 lakh each.The bureau suspects that the family acquired these properties at prices substantially below market value.“Confidential sources have also revealed that Agrawal registered the purchase of 20 villas on March 27 this year, the same day the Finance Department issued a special concessional financial package to Goyal Fashions Private Limited,” the bureau claimed.It alleged that Agrawal colluded with the company’s directors during his tenure in govt, helping the company secure undue benefits and causing substantial financial losses to the state.ACB said it also found it necessary to investigate whether he had accumulated assets disproportionate to his known sources of income in his own name and those of his family members. The agency said it had perused newspaper reports, examined a factual report from the industries department and gathered information from confidential sources before registering the inquiry against Agrawal.The bureau said preliminary investigations also found that Agrawal colluded with the company’s directors to buy villas at its Ananta resorts in his own name and those of his family members.ACB said it was also examining alleged misuse by Agrawal of his official position during past tenures as Udaipur district collector, chairperson of the Rajasthan State Pollution Control Board and additional chief secretary, Industries, among others.
Article Summary: The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) Friday registered a preliminary inquiry against senior IAS officer Shikhar Agrawal. He was serving as an additional chief secretary, industries, when he was put on awaiting posting orders (APO) status Wednesday. At the centre of the probe are alleged irregularities in the purchase of villas by him and family members.

Article Title: India ready to share its battle-tested expertise with Asean partners to boost joint capabilities: Rajnath
Article Text:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh addressing the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM)

Rajnath Singh with Australian and Japanese defence ministers

NEW DELHI: India’s extensive expertise in counter-terrorism is not theoretical classroom knowledge but it is an experience hard-earned on the ground through decades of directly confronting complex, cross-border security challenges, defence minister Rajnath Singh said in the Philippines on Thursday.Addressing the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) - Plus in Cebu, Rajnath underlined that “every strategy of India has been tested, refined and proven in the crucible of real-world operations” and that India stands fully prepared to share its practical, battle-tested experience with ADMM-Plus partners through joint exercises, capacity-building programmes, and robust intelligence sharing to strengthen collective capabilities. He reaffirmed the country’s commitment to collective regional security and eradication of terrorism in all its forms.Rajnath said this proactive, battle-tested doctrine was decisively demonstrated during Operation Sindoor, when India dismantled terrorist infrastructure and enforced a non-negotiable red line against state-sponsored terror. He stressed that counter-terrorism remains an important area of cooperation under the ADMM-Plus framework, and India and Malaysia are co-chairing the experts’ working group on counter-terrorism for the 2024 to 2027 cycle.Rajnath highlighted that by deploying frontline warships, India has successfully escorted thousands of merchant vessels and thwarted dozens of high-seas hijackings, extending protection to commercial shipping irrespective of flag or nationality. He termed the security of commercial shipping as India’s responsibility. “In an era where global trade routes face complex transnational threats, India stands ready to move beyond rhetoric. There is a need for effective action, regular operational presence and international cooperation. India will continue serving as a reliable net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and the wider Indo-Pacific,” he said.The minister highlighted the importance of youth engagement in strengthening India-ASEAN defence cooperation, stating that the shared demographic profile and aspirations of the young populations provide a strong foundation for deeper regional partnership. He proposed the establishment of a dedicated defence ‘Youth Bridge’ to enhance institutional people-to-people connectivity, promote digital innovation and facilitate capacity building in line with ADMM-Plus initiatives.On the sidelines of ADMM-Plus, Rajnath met Japanese minister of defence Shinjiro Koizumi, and Australian minister for defence Richard Marles and posted a picture with them. “JAI: Japan, Australia, India”, the defence Minister posted on X, with him holding hands of both Marles and Koizumi, as he stood in the middle.At the forum, the minister reiterated that India attaches importance to ASEAN centrality and a secure, open, inclusive, resilient and rule-based Indo-Pacific, where peace and stability are not just aspirations but a result of collective commitment. He stated that its strategic engagement with ASEAN is long-term and rooted in shared interests, mutual respect and practical cooperation. He recalled that the second ASEAN-India defence ministers’ informal meeting in Kuala Lumpur in Oct last year reaffirmed the commitment to advancing the defence and security components of the ASEAN-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and the ASEAN-India Plan of Action for 2026 to 2030.On the theme of 13th ADMM-Plus ‘Navigating Our Future, Together’, Rajnath stated it resonates with India’s foreign and defence policy paradigms as well as its civilisational ethos of ‘Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah’ (May all beings be happy) that reflects the aspiration for the happiness, prosperity, and well-being of all the people across the world. “This theme reminds us that our greatest strength lies in our solidarity and the shared ability to leverage our geographic, economic and strategic diversity. India believes in an international system built on mutual trust, co-operation, and collective responsibility. It is this precise collaborative spirit that empowers us to overcome the challenges to peace and order,” he said.The minister described maritime cooperation as crucial to India’s engagement with ASEAN during 2026, highlighting New Delhi’s designation of 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation and the conduct of the second ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise. He emphasised that India does not merely preach the tenets of international maritime law; it is a steadfast practitioner of global laws concerning maritime security. “Our commitment to ensuring the freedom of navigation and safeguarding global Sea Lines of Communication is backed by a continuous, decades-long operational legacy. Since 2008, the Indian Navy has maintained an uninterrupted, active presence in highly volatile corridors like the Gulf of Aden, without coercion or unilateral actions that undermine the rights of other nations,” he said.Rajnath said India’s emphasis on the rule of law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and its advocacy for freedom of navigation and overflight are not directed against any country but are meant to safeguard the collective interests of all regional stakeholders who depend on open sea lanes and stable maritime governance.
Article Summary: Rajnath Singh underlined that “every strategy of India has been tested, refined and proven in the crucible of real-world operations’ He reaffirmed the country’s commitment to collective regional security and eradication of terrorism in all its forms.

Article Title: Delhi-NCR feels winter chill after overnight rain, AQI improves to 'moderate'
Article Text:
Delhi's AQI which remained above 200 in the 'poor' category on Wednesday and Thursday, improved to 133 in the 'moderate' category





NEW DELHI: Delhi-NCR experienced a shift in its weather after overnight incessant rain lashed the city, bringing an unmistakable nip to the air and signalling the early onset of winter.Visuals from key locations, including Hazrat Nizamuddin railway station and the Jamia Millia Islamia area, showed rain-soaked roads and steady showers as dark clouds covered the city late on Thursday night.The rainfall also brought some relief from pollution. Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI), which remained above 200 in the 'poor' category on Wednesday and Thursday, improved to 133 in the 'moderate' category at 4am on Friday, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a yellow alert for Delhi and adjoining National Capital Region (NCR) districts on October 29, forecasting rain and thunderstorms over the next 24 to 48 hours.Weather conditions are expected to improve thereafter, with clear skies likely in early November.According to the Regional Meteorological Centre in New Delhi, widespread weather activity is expected across Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad, Gurgaon and Faridabad.The forecast indicates generally cloudy skies, with one or two spells of light to moderate rain accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning in several areas. Isolated locations may receive heavy rainfall during the night.The wet spell is expected to continue on October 30, with very light to light rain at several places and moderate showers during the morning and forenoon hours.By October 31, skies are likely to become partly cloudy, with no weather warnings in place. The IMD has forecast mainly clear skies and stable conditions across the region on November 1 and 2.
Article Summary: Overnight incessant rain lashed the city, bringing an unmistakable nip to the air and signalling the early onset of winter. Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI), which remained above 200 in the 'poor' category on Wednesday and Thursday, improved to 133 on Friday. Weather conditions are expected to improve thereafter, with clear skies likely in early November.

Article Title: Man buys Ola electric scooter for Rs 1.02 lakh in January 2024, finds parking lock faulty on day 1 and vehicle stops working on day 2; consumer forum orders company to replace scooter or refund full a
Article Text:
Image Enhanced Using AI (Used For Representational Purpose Only)





AGRA: An electric scooter that developed problems on the day it was purchased and stopped working completely the following day has landed Ola Electric Technology Pvt Ltd in trouble, with an Aligarh consumer forum directing the company to replace the vehicle or refund its purchase price of Rs 1,02,505 with 10% annual interest.The Aligarh District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum also directed the company and its authorised service centre to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.Vaibhav Sharma bought the electric scooter from an Ola showroom on Jan 31, 2024, for Rs 1,02,505. On the first day itself, the vehicle's parking lock became engaged and could not be unlocked, while its storage compartment failed to lock after being opened.Sharma reported the defects to the Aligarh service centre and emailed the company's customer support team on Feb 1, his lawyer Shivam Nayak said on Thursday. The scooter stopped working completely the following day.According to the consumer forum's order, Sharma visited the service centre repeatedly on Feb 2, 3, 5 and 6, but the problems remained unresolved. He eventually had to leave the scooter at the workshop.On Feb 9, Sharma discovered that the company had closed his complaints without fixing the defects. He subsequently approached the consumer forum, seeking a replacement or refund, along with compensation for financial loss and mental harassment.In their joint written statement, Ola's manufacturing and service entities claimed they had taken all necessary steps to address Sharma's concerns promptly.However, the forum observed that the companies had not specifically denied the defects, Sharma's repeated visits to the service centre or the complaints he had raised. It noted that Sharma had supported his allegations through an affidavit, while the opposite parties had failed to specifically rebut them.In its order dated Oct 16, 2026, the consumer forum, comprising president Hasnain Qureshi and member Purnima Singh Rajpoot, held that Sharma had established his case against the company and its authorised service centre.
Article Summary: Vaibhav Sharma bought the electric scooter from an Ola showroom on Jan 31, 2024, for Rs 1,02,505. On the first day itself, the vehicle's parking lock became engaged and could not be unlocked. Sharma reported the defects to the Aligarh service centre and emailed the company's customer support team.

Hailstorms are possible in parts of western Uttar Pradesh.Delhi witnessed a sudden change in weather overnight as scattered rainfall and thunderstorms brought some relief from lingering air pollution. Article Title: By year-end, Delhi Metro's Magenta Line extension will connect four major stretches
Article Text:
Delhi Metro Magenta Line

Peragarhi to become interchange station





NEW DELHI: The six-km Keshopur-Pushpanjali section — part of the 29-km Janakpuri West and RK Ashram Marg corridor and comprising six elevated stations — on Magenta Line is nearing completion. Its trial run is set to begin next month after which it is expected to open to public by 2026-end.Peeragarhi, an interchange station, will link this section to the existing Green Line. Other stations on this stretch include Keshopur, Paschim Vihar, Mangolpuri, West Enclave and Pushpanjali.With its opening, the Magenta Line extension will connect four major stretches: Green Line at Peeragarhi, Red Line at Pitampura, Yellow Line at Haiderpur Badli Mor and Pink Line at Majlis Park. “The Keshopur-Pushpanjali section is a key step in Delhi Metro Rail Corporation‘s (DMRC) Phase-IV expansion to improve accessibility and provide a direct, seamless link from northwest Delhi to south Delhi, Noida and IGI Airport Terminal 1,” said an official.“Civil work on the entire stretch has been fully completed and finishing touches are being given,” the official said.The station buildings have been designed with passenger convenience in mind.All stations, except Peeragarhi, have three levels: ground floor, first floor for concourse and second for platforms. “Peeragarhi has a different design as it is an interchange station. Its ground floor is for concourse, first has both concourse and platform facilities, and second accommodates a 160-metre-long foot overbridge connecting it to the Green Line station,” said the official, adding that a crossover has been provided on this stretch for train operations.These six stations will have modern amenities like passenger information display, public address systems, automatic fare collection gates, lifts, escalators and platform screen doors. “The corridor will be equipped with communication-based train control signalling and an unattended train operation system for greater safety, reliability and efficiency,” said the official.Entry and exit points have been planned according to the requirements of each station. Mangolpuri will have three entry and exit points, the most on this stretch, while West Enclave will have two, including an emergency exit.The Janakpuri West-RK Ashram Marg corridor comprises 22 stations. Two of its sections have already been commissioned: Janakpuri West to Krishna Park Extension (1.8 km) on Jan 5 this year and Deepali Chowk to Majlis Park (9.9 km) on March 8. With the opening of the latest six-km section, Magenta Line will become 55 km long and have 39 stations.Once the entire Janakpuri West-RK Ashram section becomes operational and after the addition of Central Vista corridor (RK Ashram to Indraprastha) and Indraprastha to Inderlok corridor, the total length of Magenta Line will further increase to 88.4 km, making it the longest in DMRC network. It will run all the way from Botanical Garden to Inderlok as a fully driverless corridor.
Article Summary: The six-km Keshopur-Pushpanjali section is part of the 29-km Janakpuri West and RK Ashram Marg corridor. Its trial run is set to begin next month after which it is expected to open to public by 2026-end. The Magenta Line extension will connect four major stretches.

Article Title: Diljit Dosanjh concert: Delhi Metro services will run till midnight on October 30 to facilitate spectators, while traffic curbs will remain in place around Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium from 1pm to midnigh

Traffic restrictions around JLN Stadium from 1pm

Metro stations and routes for concertgoers

NEW DELHI: Delhi Metro services will be extended till midnight on Friday (October 30) across its network, except the Airport Express Line and Rapid Metro, Gurugram, to facilitate the movement of around 70,000 spectators expected to attend singer Diljit Dosanjh’s concert at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) said additional train trips would be operated to help concertgoers return home after the event. Standby trains will also be kept ready to handle any unexpected surge in passenger traffic.The timings for purchasing QR tickets through the Delhi Metro Sarthi mobile app will also be extended by an hour in view of the revised service timings, the DMRC said.Additional staff, customer service personnel and customer facilitation agents will be deployed at JLN Stadium Metro station and key interchange stations to guide commuters and manage passenger movement.Security arrangements will also be strengthened at the station, with additional personnel, door frame metal detectors and enhanced screening measures to ensure the orderly movement of passengers.JLN Stadium Metro station, located on the Violet Line connecting Kashmere Gate and Raja Nahar Singh, is the nearest station to the concert venue. The DMRC has encouraged concertgoers to use Metro services to reach the stadium and return home, saying this would provide a convenient mode of transport and reduce dependence on private vehicles.Traffic restrictions will be in place on several roads around Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium from 1pm until midnight on Friday for the 'Aura India Tour 2026' concert, the Delhi Traffic Police said.According to a traffic advisory, six diversion points have been identified, with two additional points to be activated if required.Bhishm Pitamah Marg, Lodhi Road, Lala Lajpat Rai Marg between Defence Colony and Lodhi Colony Flyover, Arch Bishop Marg, 4th Avenue Road and 5th Avenue Road are among the stretches where traffic movement will be affected.Restrictions will also be imposed on the Barapullah Flyover stretch between INA and Jangpura Metro Gate 2, Dayal Singh College Road and internal roads in CGO Complex and Lodhi Colony.At the Lodhi Road-Dayal Singh College Road intersection, vehicles will not be allowed to enter Dayal Singh College Road. Traffic on Lodhi Road will continue towards Lodhi Flyover or Aurobindo Marg. Diversions will also be enforced at intersections on Lala Lajpat Rai Marg and Bhishm Pitamah Marg to regulate movement towards the stadium.The traffic police has advised spectators to use the Metro to avoid congestion around the stadium.Passengers can use the Violet Line to reach JLN Stadium or Jangpura Metro stations for Gates 13, 14 and 17. Those travelling on the Yellow Line can get off at INA or Jor Bagh and use designated drop-off points for Gates 3, 6 and 8.Commuters travelling from the Yellow Line have also been advised to use the Kushak Nallah Bus Depot red light as a designated drop-off point.Concertgoers travelling by taxis, auto-rickshaws and app-based cabs will have to use designated pick-up and drop-off locations. The traffic police has identified the following points:Taxis, auto-rickshaws and app-based cabs will not be allowed to halt or park along roadsides near the venue.There will be no parking facility for the general public at or around the stadium, the traffic police said.Limited parking will be available for special invitees at Sunehri Pula Bus Depot and the Dayal Singh College parking area. Motorists have been advised against roadside parking and halting near the venue.Emergency and medical vehicles will be given priority and provided obstruction-free passage during the restrictions.Commuters have been advised to allow extra travel time, plan their journeys in advance, follow instructions issued by traffic personnel and avoid roadside parking near the stadium.For assistance, commuters can contact the Delhi Traffic Police helpline at 1095. In case of emergencies, they can call 112.
Article Summary: Delhi Metro services will be extended till midnight on Friday (October 30) except Airport Express Line and Rapid Metro, Gurugram. Around 70,000 spectators expected to attend singer Diljit Dosanjh’s concert at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. Traffic police have advised spectators to use the Metro to avoid congestion around the stadium.

Article Title: Mumbai man books Panvel flat for Rs 50 lakh in 2015, waits nearly 10 years for possession; consumer commission orders developer to refund Rs 86 lakh with 9% interest
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





MUMBAI: Observing that a flat purchaser “cannot be expected to wait indefinitely” for possession and that the developer’s failure to hand over possession by the agreed deadline amounted to deficiency in service, a district consumer commission has directed M/s Soundlines Eco Homes and its partners to jointly and severally refund Rs 86.37 lakh (inclusive of interest) to a homebuyer over delayed possession in the “Sound Delight” project at Panvel. The commission allowed the complaint filed by Mulund resident Tapan Visaria. The pay out included the paid amount of Rs 45 lakh alongwith nine percent annual interest calculated from Dec 31, 2016, the contractual date of possession, until actual realization. He will also receive Rs 75,000 towards costs of litigation and mental agony.The commission refused to separately award Rs 5.23 lakh towards interest paid on the housing loan, relying on the Supreme Court’s decision. It was observed that the complainant had independently availed of a loan from the State Bank of India and was contractually liable to repay the loan with applicable interest. “The mere fact that the complainant incurred interest expenditure to arrange funds for purchasing the flat does not, by itself, make the opposite parties liable to reimburse that expenditure,” the Commission said while rejecting that head of claim.Visaria had booked the flat measuring 876 sq ft. carpet area, on the third floor of D-Wing in the project at Village Aashte, Taluka Panvel, District Raigad, for a total consideration of Rs 50.52 lakh. The agreement for sale was executed on Aug 7, 2015 and subsequently registered. According to the complainant, the developer had promised possession on or before Dec 31, 2016, but repeatedly extended the timeline, with the MahaRERA website later reflecting an extension up to Sept 30, 2026.The complainant alleged that he paid around Rs 45.45 lakh towards the flat consideration, apart from Rs 1.38 lakh towards VAT, GST and other taxes, Rs 2.53 lakh towards stamp duty and Rs 30,000 towards registration charges. He also claimed that amenities advertised in the project brochure, including an entrance gate with waterfall, clubhouse, rooftop shamiyana, amphitheatre and children’s play area, were either cancelled or not provided as promised.The opposite parties, including the partnership firm and its partners did not appear despite service of notices. The matter was therefore proceeded ex parte by order dated April 16, 2024. Taking note of the unrebutted material placed by the complainant, the commission said the agreement, bank statements, demand letters, email correspondence, photographs and loan interest certificate established that the flat had been booked and substantial payment had been made. “The evidence on record establishes that the opposite parties failed to deliver possession within the agreed period and have not furnished any satisfactory explanation for the delay. Such failure amounts to deficiency in service,” the commission held.
Article Summary: A district consumer commission has directed M/s Soundlines Eco Homes and its partners to jointly and severally refund Rs 86.37 lakh. The commission allowed the complaint filed by Mulund resident Tapan Visaria. The pay out included the paid amount of Rs 45 lakh alongwith nine percent annual interest calculated from Dec 31, 2016, the contractual date of possession.
